record.where: Verification: the economy dynamics (24) and its subjects — clauses from The economy (what a delivery is now), v3.0, and the save line of the build's header

clauses.text: needs and moods set boards and pay
stock fills and drains
the wire flows and is multiplied by roads and porters
dimming, star loss, going quiet and relighting
chain bonuses
letters, crises, night
skill verbs, save migration
Every station has a population, three or four needs and a few things it makes

figure.note: every town has people and three or four needs, each on a 0–100 shelf

clauses.text: The opening is true to the fiction: Elm Farm is out of medicine (8), Haven is eating its reserves (31), the Mill is hungry (18), the Greenhouse is nearly out of seed

figure.note: a new valley's shelves read 8, 31 and 18 (the Greenhouse's seed 20)

clauses.text: Haven makes tools and textiles; Elm grows food and seed; the Greenhouse grows medicine and filters; the Mill makes parts and tools; the Quarry tools; Relay Hill lumen cells; the Foundry coolant and parts; the Pharos makes nothing and needs everything
Stock sets a mood — critical < 15, wanting < 35, steady < 65, thriving

figure.note: read at the edges: 14.99 critical, 15 wanting, 34.99 wanting, 35 steady, 64.99 steady, 65 thriving

clauses.text: mood sets the price: ×2.2 / ×1.5 / ×1.0 / nothing

figure.note: the same crate pays ×2.2, ×1.5 and ×1 by the shelf it lands on; a thriving shelf is never posted

clauses.text: A station never posts an order for a need it is thriving on
who among the places you know is short of it, how badly
Stock for each need sits on a 0–100 bar that drains with time (0.035/s × population; the unconnected ration at half rate)

figure.note: a minute costs lit Haven 2.1, the Mill off the wire 0.945, the Pharos 1.26

clauses.text: A delivered crate adds 28

figure.note: 20 → 48 for a crate, 20 → 76 for two, 90 → 100 at the cap

clauses.text: When a station is connected, what its connected neighbours make flows to it on its own (0.06/s per feeding maker) — more than its people consume, so a connected pair sustains itself and its stock climbs to full

figure.note: DATA's wireFlow 0.06; Haven's rations +0.025 a second net, Elm's tools +0.032, both full an hour on

clauses.text: The player is told this the first time it happens
A paved road between two stations multiplies that flow (×1.6 partial

figure.note: measured off the Mill's shelf: a partial road adds by the share paved — ×1.2 for one stretch of three, ×1.4 for two — under the ×1.6 a partial road approaches (the record does not say which it meant)

clauses.text: ×2.2 complete

figure.note: the Saddle Road complete carries ×2.2, measured and multiplied

clauses.text: a chartered route porter adds ×1 more

figure.note: ×2 on the bare road, ×3.2 on the complete one; a hungry porter adds nothing

clauses.text: A connected station critical on a need that a known maker could supply dims (its light radius shrinks by a quarter, so the safe ground shrinks)

figure.note: ground eight-tenths of the reach out, lit before, falls dark (a shrink past a fifth); the coverage drops

clauses.text: Shortages of goods nobody you know makes are rationed, not held against you
If the wire is not already closing that shortage (no connected maker), four minutes of it costs a star — "people are leaving"

figure.note: two stars held at 239 s, one by 242 s

clauses.text: and with no stars left the station goes quiet: off the wire, light out, and every lit terminal posts a Relight X core order
Several crates landed in one trip pay a rising chain bonus (+15% per further stop, capped ×1.6)

figure.note: ×1, ×1.15, ×1.30, ×1.45, then ×1.6 from the fifth stop on

clauses.text: Letters go everywhere people are
light, half pay

figure.note: the post takes no fee (v3.16): the run handed over at Elm Farm paid nothing

clauses.text: and each one read aloud on delivery (24 lines from the valley)

figure.note: the line read on the slip is one of DATA.letterLines' twenty-four

clauses.text: A place's mailbag refills only every ~5–8 minutes once carried off; they are proof, not income

figure.note: the next run posts between 5 and 8 game-minutes after a bagful is carried off (5.3)

clauses.text: Crises (events after three stations are lit) empty a station's best-stocked need in one stroke

figure.note: a hundred and fifty rolls with two lit bring none; with three, one comes

clauses.text: A day is 8 minutes; the last 40% is night
wraiths wake in thinner mist, the cold bites harder
and the HUD says so
Rigging 2 lays a field ladder from 8 scrap when none is packed

figure.note: the crate on the back 10 → 2, the bank untouched

clauses.text: Hearthcraft 2 cooks a warm meal anywhere
Salvage 2 (or a Scavenger) pings scrap and lumen on the compass
v1/v2 saves migrate and are seeded with stock

checks.title: THE MOODS SET THE BOARD, IN MOTION
LETTERS GO EVERYWHERE PEOPLE ARE, READ ALOUD (v3.16

design.what: the service rule: letters take no fee — the run is a SERVICE OF THE ORDER, paid in skill and the town's thanks
